source_span: Overall , when the results are grouped per literature reference number ( which is included in the dataset ) the average quality decreases and the standard deviation increases , indicating that differences between reported Log FC changes in literature exist and this could adversely affect model performance .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key challenge in modeling drug resistance from heterogeneous data.

fact: The model correctly classifies HIV drug resistance response in 84% of cases overall, with accuracy varying by drug class (PI 85%, NNRTI 89%, NRTI 79%).
source_span: Our model classifies the response correctly in 84% of the cases ( Table 5 ) . The average performance when grouped per individual drug class was very good ( PI 85% , NNRTI 89% and NRTI 79% ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the key performance metric demonstrating the model's clinical relevance.

fact: The model tends to overpredict resistance rather than underpredict it, which is especially relevant in a clinical setting.
source_span: Also noteworthy is that the model bias is towards over prediction rather than under prediction , something that is not always mentioned in literature but is especially relevant in a clinical setting .
selection_reasoning: This fact addresses an important aspect of model behavior affecting clinical decision-making.

fact: This work reports the construction of robust proteochemometric (PCM) models based on 300,000 bioactivity data points measured against different HIV genotypes.
source_span: In this work we report the construction of robust PCM models, based on 300,000 bioactivity data points measured against different HIV genotypes.
selection_reasoning: Describes the main methodological advance and dataset scale central to the study.

fact: The PCM models combined resistance profiles of three HIV drug classes (PI, NNRTI, and NRTI) into three single models covering tens of thousands of different protein mutants.
source_span: Given the nature of the PCM modeling procedure employed in this work, we were able to combine all resistance profiles of the three above drug classes in three single models, hence focusing on very large target space (tens of thousands of different proteins) in this work.
selection_reasoning: Highlights the comprehensive scope of the models across multiple drug classes and mutants.

fact: The PCM models showed performance comparable to assay reliability and better than sequence-only models in both internal validation and validation on unseen data.
source_span: Both in internal validation and validation on unseen data our model showed performance comparable to assay reliability and better than sequence only models;
selection_reasoning: Indicates the improved predictive accuracy and robustness of the models, a key finding.

fact: Model interpretation identified novel resistance-conferring mutations that cause resistance to all drugs in a class, such as T216M in reverse transcriptase.
source_span: Moreover, model interpretation has been performed to identify novel resistance-conferring mutations that lead to resistance to all drugs in a class, such as T216M in the case of RT.
selection_reasoning: Provides a key biological insight derived from the models relevant to drug resistance.

fact: The models can also identify mutations that cause specific sensitivity or resistance to a single drug within a class, such as G48W causing sensitivity and G68R causing resistance in protease.
source_span: In addition, we can use these models to find mutations that lead specific sensitivity (G48W in PR) or resistance (G68R in PR) to a single drug within a class.
selection_reasoning: Demonstrates the models' utility for fine-grained mutation-drug interaction predictions.

fact: The PCM models can support personalized drug regimen predictions by reliably predicting clinical resistance.
source_span: Another application of our models is the support of personalized drug regimen predictions. We have shown that our models are able to predict clinical resistance with a high degree of reliability.
selection_reasoning: Shows the translational relevance of the models for clinical decision-making.

fact: The models achieved a 95% correct classification percentage (CCP) when predicting clinical response for Antivirogram assay data, which they were trained on.
source_span: This reliability is formed by a 95% CCP when predicting clinical response for Antivirogram data, which is the assay models were trained on,
selection_reasoning: Quantifies the high accuracy of the models on training assay data, supporting their validity.

fact: The models achieved up to 81% CCP when predicting clinical response for unknown mutants and 84% CCP for clinical isolates from diverse sources, demonstrating robustness and predictive power.
source_span: Furthermore, the CCP and is as high as 81% when predicting clinical response for unknown mutants. ... Finally, the CCP is 84% when predicting clinical response for clinical isolates obtained from very diverse sources (including historical literature data and data from different assays), indicating that the model is robust and predictive.
selection_reasoning: Highlights the models' ability to generalize to new and diverse clinical data, a key significance.

fact: The improved performance of PCM models is attributed to training on a large co-linked dataset and encoding full sequences using physicochemical properties rather than just mutation presence or absence.
source_span: We attribute the better performance of PCM to two reasons. Firstly our models are trained on a very large co-linked dataset. ... The second reason is related to the first, as the encoding of the full sequences using physicochemical properties rather than presence or absence of mutations allows for a better similarity measure between two sequences.
selection_reasoning: Explains the methodological innovations underlying the model's success.

fact: The main dataset was obtained from Virco and consisted of protease and reverse transcriptase mutants with fold change data in pIC50 from the AVG assay collected up to January 2011.
source_span: The main dataset was obtained from Virco (Beerse, Belgium) and consisted of mutants (both PR and RT sequences) and fold change (Log FC) in pIC50 (log units) data in the AVG assay collected by Virco up to January 2011.
selection_reasoning: Provides background on the data source and type, important for understanding the study context.

fact: Sequences were encoded using Z-scales, which characterize physicochemical properties of amino acid side chains such as lipophilicity, size, and polarity.
source_span: Sequences were subsequently encoded using the first three Z-scales. The Z-scales are a previously published set of descriptors that characterize the physicochemical properties of the amino acids side chains. The resulting scales correlate to lipophilicity, size and polarity for each amino acid.
selection_reasoning: Describes a key methodological step enabling improved sequence representation.

fact: Proteochemometric (PCM) models were constructed using support vector machines to predict drug resistance based on HIV mutant sequences and drug features.
source_span: Models were constructed in the academic version of Pipeline Pilot 6 . 1 . 5 using the R-statistics package . Support vector machines ( SVM ) with a radial basis function kernel as coded in the e1071 package were used for model creation .
selection_reasoning: This describes the key modeling approach used to address the main research question about predicting drug resistance.

fact: The applicability domain of the models was determined based on the density of nearest neighbor sequences in the training set rather than on a single wild type sequence.
source_span: As our models are trained on a database of different HIV mutants , applicability domains based on a single wild type sequence are expected to perform sub optimal . Rather we choose to determine the applicability domain based on the density of the nearest neighbors in the training set .
selection_reasoning: This explains a novel or important methodological choice relevant to model reliability and interpretation.

fact: The PCM models showed robust performance with good validation parameters, improving as the training dataset size increased.
source_span: The learning curves show that the models gradually improve when trained on a larger dataset . The results show that PCM is not only able to create models on this data , but also that these models are robust with good validation parameters .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding demonstrating the effectiveness and reliability of the modeling approach.

fact: The protease inhibitor (PI) model showed the best predictive performance with a root mean square error (RMSE) below 0.30 log units when trained on 70% of the dataset.
source_span: The PI model shows the best performance , RMSE = 0 . 42 log units when trained on 5% of the full set and <0 . 30 log units when trained on 70% of the dataset .
selection_reasoning: This highlights a key quantitative result about model accuracy for an important drug class.

fact: Models trained on scrambled data showed no predictive power, confirming that the original models capture meaningful relationships between mutations and drug resistance.
source_span: Models that were trained on this scrambled set and validated on 30% the data that was kept unscrambled produced very high RMSE values ... Furthermore , the values for the R02 were very low ... Finally the cross validation parameters for the models trained on these scrambled sets demonstrated a lack of correlation ... The corresponding correlation coefficient was 0 . 00 for all three models .
selection_reasoning: This validates the model by showing that randomizing the data destroys predictive ability, supporting the significance of the original findings.

fact: In silico mutation of individual residues back to wild type allowed interpretation of the model by estimating the effect of specific mutations on drug resistance.
source_span: To determine the effect of individual residues , for each sequence each residue was mutated back to wild type in silico by replacing the descriptors of the mutant amino acid with the descriptors of the corresponding wild type residue ... The difference was interpreted as the change in pIC50 induced by that particular residue , hence providing model interpretability .
selection_reasoning: This describes a key method for understanding which mutations drive resistance, important for biological insight.

fact: Known resistance mutations were compared to model interpretations to validate the model's ability to identify mutations that increase drug resistance.
source_span: Known resistant mutations were retrieved from earlier publications by Johnson et al . and compared to our model interpretation .
selection_reasoning: This links model findings to established knowledge, supporting clinical and biological relevance.

fact: Novel mutations that increase drug resistance were identified by filtering out known mutations and selecting those with consistent negative effects on drug susceptibility.
source_span: Mutations were filtered using the following parameters: have a negative effect on the majority of drugs in a single class; occurrence in the dataset more than once; average Log FC for all compounds >0 . 4; standard deviation over this average <0 . 4 ... using literature we discarded any previously known mutations and kept those mutations that were novel .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the discovery of new resistance-associated mutations, a key scientific contribution.

fact: The study identified novel mutations that lead to an increase in drug resistance fold change on average, after excluding previously known mutations.
source_span: This provided us with a number of mutations that lead to an increase in fold change on average , again using literature we discarded any previously known mutations and kept those mutations that were novel .
selection_reasoning: Identifying novel resistance mutations is a core finding relevant to understanding drug resistance mechanisms.

fact: The dataset used to compare the performance of proteochemometric (PCM) models with sequence-only models was obtained from Van der Borght et al. and included sequences with the largest prediction errors per drug class.
source_span: The dataset we used to compare the performance of PCM models with sequence only models was obtained from Van der Borght et al . [39] From the paper the 150 sequences with the largest prediction error were selected per drug class .
selection_reasoning: Describing the dataset and comparison approach is important for understanding the study's evaluation of predictive models.

fact: The study focused on three drug classes: NNRTI, NRTI, and PI, with final datasets containing 146, 146, and 149 sequences respectively after filtering.
source_span: leading to a total of 146 NNRTI sequences , 146 NRTI sequences , and 149 PI sequences .
selection_reasoning: Specifying the drug classes and dataset sizes provides context for the scope of the analysis.

fact: The Phenosense assay is more quantitative than the AVG assay, but the correlation between their resistance measurements is not very strong for some mutations and drugs.
source_span: Prediction of the Stanford University set is of is of particular interest since the correlation between Phenosense and AVG has previously been shown not to be very strong . [63] , [64] Yet it should also be noted that the Phenosense assay is in fact more quantitative . AVG measures cell death which can be sensitive to slight differences in the state of the host cells used to grow virus . In particular for mutations M41L , M184V , and T215Y there are differences in Phenosense predictions compared with AVG . [65]
selection_reasoning: Understanding assay differences is important for interpreting resistance prediction results and their clinical relevance.

fact: The resistance profiles of drugs d4T and TDF show a Pearson's correlation coefficient below 0.8 between the Phenosense and AVG assays, indicating discrepancies between these assays.
source_span: For instance the resistance profile of d4T and TDF , have been shown to have a Pearson's correlation coefficient <0 . 8 between the two assays . [51]
selection_reasoning: Highlighting assay discrepancies for specific drugs is relevant for evaluating prediction accuracy and clinical interpretation.

fact: Sequences present in the Virco training set were removed from the Stanford reference set to avoid artificially boosting prediction results.
source_span: The reference set was downloaded from the Stanford website ( version 5 . 0 , July 30 , 2010 ) , from this set the sequences by Virco were removed ( as they are presumed to be in the training set , and this would artificially boost the results ) .
selection_reasoning: Ensuring unbiased validation by removing training data overlap is a key methodological detail.

fact: The study predicted Log fold change values for individual drug–mutant pairs and calculated validation parameters grouped by sequence, isolate, reference ID, drug, and drug class.
source_span: After we predicted the Log FC values for individual drug – mutant pairs using our models , the validation parameters were calculated grouped by: Sequence ID ( average and standard deviation ) , per Isolate ( average and standard deviation ) , per Reference ID ( average and standard deviation ) , per drug ( average and standard deviation ) , per class ( total ) , and per individual drug ( total )
selection_reasoning: Describing the prediction and validation approach is central to understanding the study's evaluation of model performance.

fact: Resistance was classified using clinical cut-offs from the Stanford website and AVG values from Virco, and clinical cut-off performance (CCP) was calculated including fractions of overpredicted and underpredicted clinical responses.
source_span: Resistance was also classified using clinical cut-offs ( CCOs ) , here we used the values provided on the Stanford website and the values from AVG were obtained from Virco ( supporting Table S10 and supporting Table S11 ) . Subsequently CCP was calculated as a fraction of the total , in addition the fraction of overpredicted clinical response ( resistance is predicted higher than measured experimentally ) and underpredicted clinical response ( resistance is predicted lower than measured experimentally ) is included .
selection_reasoning: Using clinical cut-offs and evaluating prediction errors in clinical resistance classification is important for translational relevance.

fact: Staphylococcus aureus is the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections (SSTIs) in humans.
source_span: Staphylococcus aureus is the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections ( SSTIs ) in humans [1 , 2] with S . aureus SSTIs resulting in over 11 million outpatient visits and almost 500 , 000 hospital admissions in the United States annually [3] .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides essential background on the clinical importance of S. aureus SSTIs, motivating the study.

fact: S. aureus SSTIs often form cutaneous abscesses that limit antibiotic penetration and efficacy.
source_span: S . aureus SSTIs routinely manifest as cutaneous abscesses which limit the penetration and efficacy of antibiotics [4] .
selection_reasoning: This explains a key clinical challenge in treating S. aureus SSTIs, justifying the need for alternative therapies.

fact: Community-acquired methicillin-resistant S. aureus (CA-MRSA) skin infections are increasing in healthy individuals and are difficult to treat due to antibiotic resistance.
source_span: Community-acquired methicillin resistant S . aureus ( CA-MRSA ) skin infections are increasing in frequency in healthy individuals [5] and the treatment of these infections has become increasingly difficult due to the emergence of antibiotic resistance .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the growing public health problem and the need for new preventive strategies.

fact: An effective anti-S. aureus vaccine remains elusive, and a vaccine targeting specific clinical manifestations such as SSTIs may be necessary.
source_span: The development of an anti-S . aureus vaccine offers a potential solution to prevent infection regardless of antibiotic resistance; however , although significant efforts have been made , an effective anti-S . aureus vaccine remains elusive . Given the wide spectrum of pathologies caused by this bacterium it is unlikely that a universal anti-S . aureus vaccine will ever be realised [6] , and instead , a vaccine targeting specific clinical manifestations may need to be pursued .
selection_reasoning: This frames the rationale for focusing on SSTI-specific vaccine targets.

fact: Staphylococcus aureus expresses up to 25 different cell wall-anchored (CWA) proteins that mediate adhesion, invasion, biofilm formation, and immune evasion.
source_span: S . aureus expresses up to 25 different cell wall-anchored ( CWA ) proteins , which are covalently linked to the peptidoglycan layer by the enzyme sortase A and are primarily involved in adhesion and invasion of host cells and tissues , biofilm formation and immune evasion [8] .
selection_reasoning: This provides biological background on the virulence factors relevant to the study.

fact: Sortase A-deficient mutants lacking most CWA proteins show reduced virulence and bacterial burden in skin abscess models.
source_span: Sortase A-deficient mutants , which lack the majority of cell surface bound CWA proteins , have reduced virulence in a murine kidney abscess model [9 , 10] , while in a skin abscess model , a sortase A-deficient mutant resulted in lower bacterial burden in the skin and a significantly reduced pathology compared to wild-type infected mice [11] .
selection_reasoning: This supports the importance of CWA proteins in SSTI pathogenesis.

fact: Clumping factor B (ClfB) is a cell wall-anchored protein that facilitates S. aureus nasal colonization by binding to the cornified envelope in the anterior nares.
source_span: The cell wall-anchored protein clumping factor B ( ClfB ) has previously been shown to facilitate S . aureus nasal colonization through high affinity interactions with the cornified envelope in the anterior nares .
selection_reasoning: This introduces ClfB and its known role, setting up the study question.

fact: The role of ClfB during skin and soft tissue infection (SSTI) had not been previously investigated.
source_span: However , the role of ClfB during skin and soft tissue infection ( SSTI ) has never been investigated .
selection_reasoning: This identifies the knowledge gap addressed by the study.

fact: This study reveals a novel role for ClfB during SSTIs, showing it is crucial in determining abscess structure and bacterial burden early in infection.
source_span: This study reveals a novel role for ClfB during SSTIs . ClfB is crucial in determining the abscess structure and bacterial burden early in infection and this is dependent upon a specific interaction with the ligand loricrin which is expressed within the abscess tissue .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding central to the study's contribution.

fact: ClfB interacts specifically with the ligand loricrin, which is expressed within abscess tissue during SSTIs.
source_span: ClfB is crucial in determining the abscess structure and bacterial burden early in infection and this is dependent upon a specific interaction with the ligand loricrin which is expressed within the abscess tissue .
selection_reasoning: This identifies a key molecular mechanism underlying ClfB's role in SSTIs.

fact: Targeting ClfB with a model vaccine that induces both humoral and cellular immune responses leads to protection during S. aureus skin infection.
source_span: Targeting ClfB using a model vaccine that induced both protective humoral and cellular responses , leads to protection during S . aureus skin infection .
selection_reasoning: This finding demonstrates the translational potential of ClfB as a vaccine antigen.

fact: ClfB is identified as an important antigen for future vaccines specifically targeting S. aureus skin and soft tissue infections.
source_span: This study therefore identifies ClfB as an important antigen for future SSTI vaccines .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the study's significance and implication for vaccine development.

fact: Mice infected with a ClfB-deficient S. aureus strain formed significantly smaller abscess lesions and had reduced bacterial burden compared to mice infected with wild-type S. aureus.
source_span: Mice infected with LAC::lux ΔclfB formed significantly smaller abscess lesions on day 3–6 compared to mice infected with LAC::lux ( Fig 1A and 1B ) . The bioluminescence signal was also reduced in LAC::lux ΔclfB infected animals compared to LAC::lux infected mice ( Fig 1C and 1D ) . The reduction in bioluminescence signal was validated by quantifying the bacterial burden in the skin on day 3 ( Fig 1E ) and day 6 ( Fig 1F ) .
selection_reasoning: This experimental result directly supports the conclusion that ClfB contributes to SSTI severity.

fact: ClfB affects both the rate of abscess formation and the overall size of the abscess formed during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections.
source_span: Taken together, these results demonstrate that ClfB affects both the rate of abscess formation and the overall size of the abscess formed, which ultimately leads to greater bacterial burden in the skin.
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding linking ClfB to abscess development and bacterial burden, central to the study's main question and significance.

fact: ClfB has an important function during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections, likely exerting its effect early in the infection process.
source_span: Crucially, these results have demonstrated for the first time that ClfB has an important function during S. aureus SSTIs, likely exerting its effect early in the infection process.
selection_reasoning: This highlights the novel discovery and timing of ClfB's role, important background and main conclusion.

fact: During nasal colonization, Staphylococcus aureus binding to the squamous epithelium is facilitated by the interaction between ClfB and the squamous cell envelope protein loricrin.
source_span: During nasal colonization, S. aureus binding to the squamous epithelium of the anterior nares is facilitated via the interaction between ClfB and the squamous cell envelope protein loricrin.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the known ClfB-loricrin interaction, providing biological context for the study.

fact: Loricrin is present in the epidermal layer and in the abscess wall structure during Staphylococcus aureus subcutaneous abscess formation.
source_span: At 48 h post-infection loricrin is clearly visible in the epidermal layer of the skin, which is to be expected as it is a major component of the cornified envelope. Interestingly, it is also detected in the abscess wall structure following challenge with both LAC::lux and LAC::lux ΔclfB.
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the relevance of loricrin in the infected tissue, linking to the ClfB-loricrin interaction during infection.

fact: Loricrin-deficient mice form significantly smaller abscesses and have reduced bacterial burden during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections compared to wild-type mice.
source_span: Lor-/- mice formed significantly smaller abscesses compared to WT mice and had reduced bioluminescence, indicating the presence of loricrin is important for abscess formation and bacterial burden during S. aureus SSTIs.
selection_reasoning: This finding demonstrates the functional importance of loricrin in abscess formation and bacterial growth, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: Abscess formation is impaired in loricrin-deficient mice at 12 hours post infection, with less well-structured and smaller abscesses formed.
source_span: Importantly, it can be seen that abscess formation is impaired in Lor-/- mice at 12 hours post infection with overall less well-structured and smaller abscesses being formed.
selection_reasoning: This supports the early role of loricrin in abscess development, reinforcing the timing and mechanism of infection.

fact: In wild-type mice, infection with Staphylococcus aureus lacking ClfB results in smaller abscess lesions and reduced bacterial burden compared to infection with wild-type bacteria.
source_span: WT mice that received LAC::lux ΔclfB formed smaller abscess lesions and had significantly reduced bioluminescence compared to WT mice that received LAC::lux which was confirmed by quantifying bacterial burden in the skin.
selection_reasoning: This directly links ClfB expression to virulence and abscess severity, a core experimental finding.

fact: In loricrin-deficient mice, there is no significant difference in abscess lesion size or bacterial burden between infection with Staphylococcus aureus expressing ClfB and bacteria lacking ClfB.
source_span: There was no significant difference in abscess lesion area, bioluminescence or skin CFUs between Lor-/- mice that received LAC::lux or LAC::lux ΔclfB.
selection_reasoning: This shows that loricrin is required for ClfB-dependent virulence, clarifying the mechanism of interaction.

fact: Expression of loricrin within the tissue during abscess formation facilitates the binding of Staphylococcus aureus via ClfB, contributing to the formation of a robust abscess.
source_span: Taken together these data suggest that expression of loricrin within the tissue during abscess formation facilitates the binding of S. aureus specifically via ClfB, thus contributing to the formation of a robust abscess.
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the key mechanistic insight linking loricrin and ClfB to abscess formation.

fact: Pre-incubation of Staphylococcus aureus with recombinant loricrin loop L2v reduces abscess lesion area and bacterial burden during skin infection in mice.
source_span: Mice that received LAC::lux+L2v had reduced abscess lesion area compared to the LAC::lux+GST group. In addition, bioluminescence signal was reduced throughout the infection period in LAC::lux+L2v infected mice compared to mice that received LAC::lux+GST and this reduction in bioluminescence was confirmed with a significant decrease in the bacterial burden in the skin on day 3 and 6 post-infection.
selection_reasoning: This demonstrates a potential therapeutic approach by blocking ClfB-loricrin interaction to reduce infection severity.

fact: Vaccination with ClfB combined with the TLR9 agonist CpG induces antigen-specific cellular and humoral immune responses in mice.
source_span: Immunization with ClfB in combination with CpG drove a significant increase in ClfB-specific IFNγ, IL-17 and IL-22 producing CD4+ T cells by inguinal lymph node cells compared to CpG-immunized mice. ClfB-specific CD8+ T cells producing IFNγ, IL-17 and IL-22 were also increased in the ILN of ClfB-vaccinated groups compared to the adjuvant alone group. Vaccination with ClfB also induced significantly elevated ClfB-specific serum IgG titres in mice compared to the control group.
selection_reasoning: This is a key translational finding showing that ClfB can be targeted by vaccination to elicit immune responses.

fact: Antibodies induced by ClfB vaccination inhibit the binding of ClfB-expressing bacteria to loricrin.
source_span: We confirmed that these antibodies were functional by investigating their ability to inhibit L. lactis expressing ClfB to bind to immobilised loricrin.
selection_reasoning: This supports the functional relevance of the vaccine-induced antibodies, linking immune response to mechanism.

fact: ClfB is a surface protein of Staphylococcus aureus that facilitates nasal colonization by binding to host ligands loricrin and cytokeratin 10.
source_span: Previous to this study , the main function attributed to ClfB was in facilitating S . aureus nasal colonization due to its ability to bind host ligands loricrin and cytokeratin 10 in the anterior nares [13–15].
selection_reasoning: Provides essential background on ClfB's known role before this study, helping understand the significance of new findings.

fact: This study identifies ClfB as a virulence factor that contributes to the pathogenesis of Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections (SSTIs).
source_span: This study identifies , for the first time , an important role for ClfB in the pathogenesis of SSTIs and provides proof-of-concept that ClfB represents a good candidate antigen for inclusion in next-generation vaccines targeting S . aureus SSTI.
selection_reasoning: States the main novel finding and significance of the study regarding ClfB's role in SSTIs.

fact: Using a ClfB mutant strain of the clinically relevant CA-MRSA USA300, the study demonstrates that ClfB is important for early abscess formation during skin infection.
source_span: Using a clfB mutant in the clinically relevant CA-MRSA USA300 strain , LAC::lux , we demonstrate that ClfB is a virulence determinant during S . aureus skin infection . Crucially , ClfB appears to exert its effect early during the infection process during initial formation of the abscess.
selection_reasoning: Describes a key experimental approach and finding linking ClfB to early infection stages.

fact: Loricrin, a host ligand for ClfB, is present not only in the outer skin layers but also within the abscess wall during infection, suggesting it facilitates bacterial binding and abscess development.
source_span: Immunohistochemistry analysis revealed that loricrin , an important ligand for ClfB , was present in the outermost layer of the skin , the corneal layer , as expected; however , loricrin also appeared to be present within the wall of the skin abscess structure of LAC::lux infected mice .
selection_reasoning: Explains the biological mechanism by which ClfB promotes infection, important for understanding pathogenesis.

fact: Loricrin-deficient mice infected with S. aureus develop smaller abscesses with lower bacterial burden and reduced pathology compared to wild-type mice, indicating the importance of the ClfB-loricrin interaction in SSTIs.
source_span: Lor-/- mice infected s . c . with LAC::lux formed significantly smaller abscess , with lower bacterial burden and reduced pathology compared to WT infected mice , suggesting that the interaction between S . aureus and loricrin is crucial during SSTIs.
selection_reasoning: Provides functional evidence that the ClfB-loricrin interaction is critical for infection severity.

fact: Blocking the ClfB-loricrin interaction in vivo with recombinant loricrin reduces bacterial burden and abscess size during S. aureus skin infection.
source_span: Furthermore , the interaction between S . aureus and loricrin could be blocked in vivo using recombinant loricrin . Pre-incubation with recombinant loricrin L2v abolished the ability of ClfB to bind to native ligands in the skin . Throughout the infection period , mice infected with LAC::lux pre-incubated with L2v had reduced bacterial burden and abscess lesion size compared to the control group .
selection_reasoning: Demonstrates a potential therapeutic approach targeting the ClfB-loricrin interaction.

fact: Vaccination with ClfB combined with the CpG adjuvant induces strong antigen-specific cellular immune responses, including CD4+ and CD8+ T cells producing IFNγ, IL-17, and IL-22.
source_span: Immunization with ClfB+CpG induced significant expansion of antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells capable of producing IFNγ , IL-17 and IL-22 .
selection_reasoning: Describes the key immunological response induced by the vaccine candidate.

fact: Vaccination with ClfB combined with CpG also induces significant levels of ClfB-specific neutralizing antibodies in mice.
source_span: Vaccination with ClfB+CpG also activated humoral immune responses by inducing significant levels of ClfB-specific neutralizing antibodies compared to controls .
selection_reasoning: Shows that the vaccine activates both arms of the immune system, important for protection.

fact: Mice vaccinated with ClfB plus CpG adjuvant develop significantly smaller abscess lesions and have reduced bacterial burden during Staphylococcus aureus skin infection compared to controls.
source_span: Mice vaccinated with ClfB in combination with CpG developed significantly smaller abscess lesions throughout the 6-day infection period compared to those vaccinated with adjuvant alone ... and the bacterial burden in the skin of ClfB vaccinated mice was decreased throughout the course of infection as measured by bioluminescence .
selection_reasoning: Demonstrates the protective efficacy of the ClfB vaccine candidate against skin infection.

fact: Vaccination with CpG adjuvant alone does not provide protection against Staphylococcus aureus skin infection.
source_span: Immunization with CpG alone offered no protection as compared to a PBS control group .
selection_reasoning: Establishes that the antigen ClfB is necessary for vaccine efficacy, not the adjuvant alone.

fact: IL-17 and IL-22 cytokine responses induced by ClfB vaccination are important for protection against cutaneous Staphylococcus aureus infection by promoting neutrophil recruitment and antimicrobial peptide production.
source_span: IL-17 and IL-22 cytokine responses are known to be particularly important for protection during cutaneous infection with S . aureus through these cytokines ability to promote neutrophil recruitment to the infection site and also to drive local production of antimicrobial peptides , both important effector mechanisms for effective clearance of the bacterium .
selection_reasoning: Explains the immunological mechanism underlying vaccine-induced protection.

fact: ClfB has previously been shown to mediate Staphylococcus aureus adhesion to skin corneocytes in atopic dermatitis.
source_span: Interestingly , ClfB has also been shown to be a major player in mediating S . aureus adhesion to skin corneocytes in atopic dermatitis .
selection_reasoning: Provides additional context for ClfB's role in skin-related S. aureus interactions.

fact: This study uses CpG as an adjuvant for the ClfB vaccine because of its low reactogenicity and strong ability to stimulate immune responses, making it a promising adjuvant for future infectious disease vaccines.
source_span: This study utilised the adjuvant , CpG , which due to its low reactogenicity and strong adjuvanticity is currently considered a prime adjuvant for future vaccines against infectious diseases .
selection_reasoning: Explains the rationale for adjuvant choice relevant to vaccine development.

fact: Vaccination with ClfB combined with CpG adjuvant activates both humoral and cellular immune responses against Staphylococcus aureus.
